corrections.finding: The note at 76 s (American Record Guide review of 1937) was typed music; it reports reception, not what the music is doing.

checks.source: MEAS: item metadata and manifest read; cached MP3 MD5 (ab167f99…) matches the Archive manifest; 131.67 s; file starts at 0.4 s and ends on the final chord at about 130 s, so the side is complete. The metadata field runtime reads 00:02:23, longer than the 131.67 s file (the sister side's runtime equals its file length); not explained by the item, so treated as lead-in and run-out of the unrestored transfer. Pitch: chroma tuning about −4 to −7 cents of A = 440, so speed is plausible (no written key in the file to test against).
checks.identity: EXT: DAHR matrix BS-99538 (Victor, 4 Feb 1936, New York Studio 3, takes 1, 1A, 2, 2A; take 2 master on Victor 1799 and Gramophone DA-1560; Price as arranger from the disc label; Anderson contralto, Vehanen piano) and DAHR Victor 1799 (BS-99537 / BS-99538, release 2/1937, source Victor catalog) fetched and read. Archive item gives Victor 1799-B, matrix field 1799B (a label side, not a matrix).
checks.rights: EXT: American Record Guide vol. 2 no. 10, February 1937 (Archive scan, OCR read): review of 10-inch Victor 1799, $1.50, signed A. P. D. This independently dates publication to February 1937 at the latest. Pre-1963 EU basis is sound. Composition: Price d. 3 June 1953, EU public domain since 1 Jan 2024; US registration of 12 Aug 1937 (Price Works Catalog, E pub 63815) and its renewal were not checked; the dossier says so.
checks.notes: EXT: ARG quotations verified against the OCR text (overdone in the elaborate piano accompaniment; theatrical ending; catches the syncopation of the piano part; plays brilliantly). Price Works Catalog page read: manuscript 30 Sept 1931 (MC988b Box 1C Folder 35), annotation Arr. especially for and dedicated to Abbie Mitchell, copyright 12 Aug 1937 Gamble Hinged Music Co., Remick 1937 annotation As sung by Marian Anderson (Victor Record No. 1799). Lincoln Memorial note: the printed programme of 9 April 1939 (page images viewed) lists Gospel Train (Burleigh), Trampin’ (Boatner) and My Soul is Anchored in the Lord (Florence Price) after the intermission, At the piano Kosti Vehanen; 75,000 and six microphones from the Library of Congress post. Text of the song: Song of America (modern Hildegard edition). The Archive’s Whisper transcript is consistent with the refrain twice from about 8.5 s, a second refrain at about 38 s, I’m going to pray … until I reach the mountain top at about 60–74 s and refrains from about 100 s; the first couplet (hell) was not transcribed, so it rests on the modern edition, as the evidence line already says. Sections 0 / 36 / 92 agree with the level and novelty trace. Not an aural review. Four notes for 131.7 s (limit 4). Voice rules checked.

rights.decision: Publish on the territorial EU basis the dossier states.
rights.iaFlags: FLAGGED: item metadata carries curation [state]un-dark[/state] [comment]lawsuit temporary undark and noindex[/comment] (22 Aug 2025) and noindex: true; collections georgeblood, 78rpm. The Great 78 Project suit (UMG Recordings v. Internet Archive; Sony among the plaintiffs) was settled confidentially in September 2025 (IA blog, 15 Sept 2025; Music Business Worldwide, 16 Sept 2025). Whether this Victor 1799 side was in the complaint is unknown. The item is visible and streams; the dossier records the flag.
rights.reasoning: First publication February 1937 is documented by DAHR (Victor catalog) and by the ARG review of the same month. EU/UK recording term for 1937 expired long before the 2013 extension. US status is not established (Copyright Office: 1923–1946 recordings run to 95 years plus 5, here the end of 2037) and the dossier says that. Not a live or broadcast capture; no relabelling concern.
